note if they are clear despite the presence of cardiac silhouette enlargement.", "Correlate the anatomical finding (widened left superior mediastinum) with the physiological symptom (hypoxaemia) by considering a Persistent Left Superior Vena Cava (PLSVC) draining into the left atrium.", "Distinguish this from left heart failure (which would typically show pulmonary venous congestion) or compressive masses (which would not inherently cause shunting/hypoxaemia without airway compromise)."]}, {"category": "detection", "trigger": "When assessing the superior mediastinum on a PA chest radiograph to differentiate vascular anomalies from pathological masses.", "steps": ["Trace the contour of the left superior mediastinum looking for a smooth, tubular, or convex opacity extending inferiorly from the level of the aortic arch.", "Compare the density and margins of the widening to typical lymphadenopathy or tumors;
